newsitem.title: USA: NYC Water says sells bonds at lowest rate ever.
newsitem.headline: NYC Water says sells bonds at lowest rate ever.

text.p: The New York City Water Finance Authority, which had to clip the size of its bond sale because the market's recent volatility sliced demand, on Tuesday said it still captured the lowest rates in its 12-year history.

A Water Authority official, who declined to be named, said that approximately $75 million of the nearly $289 million of revenue bonds had been placed, counting retention orders, priority orders from institutions, and orders placed by individuals during a two-day, presale period.

The Authority had hoped to raise the size of the offering to around $365 million. However, Treasury bond prices stumbled badly last Friday, reacting to surprisingly strong economic data on payrolls and manufacturing, and the downward pressure continued this week. "We actually did a pretty good guess," the official said, noting the preliminary sales document was for a $300 million bond sale.

Still, the Water Authority said that its present value savings was about six percent. "This is a very generous savings, and in fact the lowest interest rate, when measured on true interest cost, the Water Authority has ever gotten," the Authority official said.

He noted that the bonds sold at about 50 basis points below an offering by the Authority this spring, even though this time around it had to give up around 20 to 25 basis points because of the kick-up in yields.

"It's a combination of, principally, the market, and also the improving overall credit quality of the city, and the improving credit quality of the Water Authority," the official added, noting that both Standard and Poor's Corp and Moody's Investors Service recently said the agency's debt had a positive outlook.

The Water Authority only got $15 million of institutional priority orders, a disappointing result, which ressembled the lack of demand displayed by retail investors. They only ordered $12 million of bonds during the presale period that ended on Monday. However, the official said the underwriters were confident that there was enough interest at the higher yields at which the bonds were repriced.

PaineWebber, the book-running senior manager, said it raised yields in several issues, increasing the top yield in 2021 to 5.50 percent from 5.474 percent. The bonds that were offered to individuals investors also were repriced at higher levels on Monday.
